display.title: The Ten Days of Teshuvah: Returning to Hashem Before Yom Kippur
display.summary_short: What teshuvah means: mitzvos connect us to Hashem and aveiros pull us away, and on Yom Kippur we return, fast and are forgiven.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show during the Ten Days of Teshuvah, with Yom Kippur falling on the coming Shabbos. Uncle Yossi explains that teshuvah means returning to our merciful Father in Heaven. Why return, if we never left? Because the word mitzvah also means connecting: each mitzvah joins us to Hashem, while an aveirah tears us away. Teshuvah means firmly resolving never to repeat the wrong and asking Hashem's forgiveness, and Yom Kippur is the day Hashem forgives us because we have returned with all our heart. To show how sorry we are, those of age fast (girls over twelve, boys over thirteen), and Hashem answers 'I have forgiven', inscribing us in the Book of Life for a year of health and blessing, and above all the coming of Moshiach.
display.lesson: Every mitzvah connects us to Hashem; teshuvah brings us back when we have drifted away.
